_note: Typical screening values. The contract specification, the crane manufacturer's limits and the site health-and-safety plan always take precedence. Edit these to match them.

heat_wbgt_moderate_work_acclimatised_C._source: ACGIH TLV / ISO 7243 style screening, moderate work, acclimatised workers

crane._source: typical tower-crane in-service limits; gust scaled from 10 m to hook height by the 1/7 power law

concrete._source: ACI 305R evaporation-rate guidance (Uno 1998 formula); concrete assumed warmer than air by concrete_minus_air_C
concrete._cold_source: ACI 306R cold-weather concreting: protect below about 5 C; caution below 10 C

coatings._source: ISO 8502-4: surface at least 3 C above dew point; RH at most 85 %

lightning._source: convective screening: CAPE with rain probability, and forecast rain in the hour for 'likely'; Kampala CAPE is above 1000 J/kg most hours, so CAPE alone is not a signal. Stop exposed work at the first thunder (30-30 rule).

asphalt._source: typical hot-mix asphalt and bituminous surface-dressing practice (e.g. MoWT General Specifications for Roads and Bridges): no laying or spraying in rain or on a wet surface, nor when rain is imminent; thin lifts cool fast in wind

_working_note: 8-hour working day: 08:00-17:00 with a lunch break 13:00-14:00 (break hours are not counted)

dust._source: Open-Meteo/CAMS dust concentration; a dust event reduces visibility and needs eye protection and secured materials

everyday._note: Everyday advice for the public (scripts/everyday.py): screening values from a forecast, not warnings. Official warnings come from the national weather service (in Uganda, UNMA) and local authorities.
everyday._rain_source: WMO-style intensity bands: light < 2.5 mm/h, heavy > 7.6 mm/h; 10 mm/h and more floods Kampala's low-lying roads and drains (Nakivubo, Lubigi channels) within the hour
everyday._gust_source: two-wheelers: gusts above about 36 km/h (10 m/s) push riders across lanes; above 54 km/h (15 m/s) do not ride
everyday._tent_source: typical marquee and event-tent operating guidance: secure and close up above about 35-40 km/h, evacuate above about 55 km/h; the tent supplier's rating takes precedence
everyday._heat_source: WBGT in the sun; general public outdoors, light activity (as the moderate-work screening values)
everyday._sensitive_source: stricter limits for children, older people and the unwell, who acclimatise and cool less well (guest heat at events is WBGT in the shade against the caution value)
everyday._exercise_source: ACSM heat guidance for exercise: high risk from WBGT about 28 C, cancel or modify above about 30-32 C
everyday._pm25_source: US EPA AQI breakpoints for PM2.5: 35.5 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', 55.5 'unhealthy' (1-hour values, screening only)
everyday._spray_source: pesticide-label practice: a rain-free period of about 6 h after spraying; spray in light wind (about 1-4 m/s at nozzle height; 10 m wind is higher) and avoid the heat of the day. The product label takes precedence

heat_advisory._note: Public heat advisory (scripts/heat_advisory.py): screening levels from forecast WBGT in the sun, not official warnings. Official heat warnings come from the national weather service (in Uganda, UNMA) and the health ministry.
heat_advisory._source: WBGT in the sun. Moderate from 25 C (heat starts to limit hard work for people not used to it); High from 28 C, the ISO 7243 / ACGIH limit for continuous moderate work by acclimatised workers (the construction advice uses the same value); Very high from 30 C and Extreme from 32 C, as in common WBGT flag systems (e.g. the US heat categories: red about 31, black about 32 C), where work-rest cycles and then stopping strenuous activity are advised
